sys_script.description: Before-insert/update on x_casemgmt_case: refuses any write whose subject exceeds 255 characters, description exceeds 4000, requester_name exceeds 100 or requester_email exceeds 100 - the four max_length values declared in AAP Section 0.5.7 and in the dictionary entries under ../dictionary/. Every offending field is named in its own gs.addErrorMessage() ('<label> must be <limit> characters or fewer. The value supplied is <n> characters.') and the write is cancelled with current.setAbortAction(true), so an over-length value can never be persisted by ANY write path. This closes a silent-data-loss gap: the platform enforces max_length only as an HTML maxlength attribute on forms - absent altogether on the >255-character description textarea, which accepted 4100 characters - and then cuts the value to fit at storage while reporting the save as successful, so the end of a long description was lost with nothing said to its author. Coverage measured on this instance: description is TEXT-backed and is ENFORCED here (a 4001-character description is answered HTTP 403 with the stored value unchanged; 4000 is accepted), while subject, requester_name and requester_email are VARCHAR-backed and are coerced to fit by the platform BEFORE the before rules run (a 300-character subject is answered HTTP 200 and stored at 255), so their checks below are the correct invariant but cannot fire from a coerced write; those three are bounded instead by the form's rendered maxlength attribute and by the anonymous portal endpoint's HTTP 400, and raising their declared max_length to make the value observable is prohibited by AAP Sections 0.5.7 and 0.7.1. A form-layer control cannot close this, because the Table API, import sets, fix scripts and flows write this table without rendering any attribute; a before rule is the only layer that covers every path. Order=70 places this rule FIRST in the before-rule chain, ahead of block_terminal_closed (100), set_opened_date (100), block_draft_backtransition (200), enforce_forward_transitions (250), validate_assigned_agent_membership (300), clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress (400) and set_closed_date (500), because a length violation is a property of the value and is independent of any status transition; orders 50 and 80 are reserved for sibling guards. Dual-triggered (action_insert AND action_update) because both paths can carry an over-length value. Early-returns on current.isActionAborted() so it never stacks a message on a save another rule already refused. Says nothing about empty values - the mandatory concern belongs to a separate guard. The anonymous portal path is additionally guarded, earlier and with an HTTP 400 { error, fields } body, by x_casemgmt.CasePortalService._validateSubmission(); this rule is the guarantee that holds when that path is not the writer. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals.
sys_script.name: x_casemgmt_validate_case_text_lengths
